Synopsis:
54 UK civil society groups, led by Campaign for Better Transport, are pressuring the UK government to adopt modal shift targets away from private car use toward public transport, cycling and walking. The push is framed around climate urgency following summer heatwaves and wildfires. Labour has notably dropped pre-election commitments on transport mode share targets. The government responds by citing existing investments (£4.5bn cycling/walking, £7.5bn ZEV mandate, bus fare cap) while resisting hard targets. A notable side reference is made to "oil price inflation caused by the US war on Iran."
